notes: The first installed version: a desktop shortcut, and updates from inside the app.
Copies camera, sound, stills, drone and 360 cards into a job, onto several drives at once, and checks every copy before a card is marked safe to format.
Several cards at once, one per reader, all copying at the same time.
Jobs come from the drives, or a new one can be made by hand. Folders follow one template, edited in the Folder template tab.
An ASC MHL, a CSV and an HTML report for every card.
A card copied before goes back to its own roll, and a stopped copy can be finished later.
Card readers and drives plugged in by USB, USB-C, SD, CFast or Thunderbolt now always show under Cards and removable drives, even when the reader calls itself a fixed disk.
Each card shows the camera that made it, such as Sony A7S III, when the card says.
A card that was copied and then shot on without formatting only has its new clips copied, into the roll it went to first, and checked. Nothing copied before is touched.
Every section folds, with Collapse all and Expand all.
New scroll bars, and the Roll folder button is now Open folder.
Eject cards and drives from the list, or straight from a card's result after copying.
Cards are named by their camera in the short form crews use (BMPCC 6K Pro), with the card's own name and drive below it (B001 I:\, or Local Disk J:\).
A card that's in the job twice now goes back to the copy filed under the card type you pick, then the first copy made, rather than the latest one.
The fonts are inside the app, so it looks the same with no internet.
The two steps are now Destination and Source.
Eject works: a card in a reader slot is ejected and the reader stays connected, and a reader or drive that Windows treats as a fixed disk is safely removed.
A new job made by Ingest only has a media folder (and its small _htt folder). The rest of a job's folders come from the Heart, so rushes can live on a drive of their own.
The copy panel shows where each copy goes: the card's drive, an arrow, then the destination.
New versions show up straight after they're released.
